_comment: Each tap listens on a lab-external port and forwards to a backend simulator port. The listen ports are what an attacker/scanner in the lab actually touches; the backend ports are where the real simulator processes run. Zone boundaries here are logical labels, not enforced by anything but the detection engine's cross-zone rule -- see docs/architecture.md. protocol=modbus enables function-code parsing on the first bytes of each connection. The decoy entries below point at a backend port nothing listens on (127.0.0.1:1) purely so a port sweep across this range produces a real, loggable 'connection refused' event for each port it touches -- exactly what a real network tap/span port would see for a scan against closed OT ports, without needing a full second service behind each one.
